investigacion.base:
**On current data, this would resolve NO, but only narrowly.** The latest rates are about 1,330–1,335, roughly 5–10 won (under 1%) below the 1,340 line. The trend is toward a stronger won.

**What the resolution source says now**
- **Trading Economics (last updated Oct 18, 2026):** The USD/KRW exchange rate was unchanged at 1,334.5500 on October 18, 2026. Over the past month, the South Korean Won has strengthened 2.94%, and is up by 6.10% over the last 12 months. That's about 0.4% below the threshold.
- **Metaculus FAQ:** I didn't get the page itself. It's only the definition of "credible sources" (for example Wise or Investing.com), which is used only if Trading Economics has no Oct 29 value.
- **Wise (backup source):** The rate is currently 1330.2 today, reflecting a -0.304% change since yesterday. Its 7-day range was a high of 1351.85 on 15-10-2026 and a low of 1329.55 on 19-10-2026. That 1,351.85 figure doesn't fit the other sources and may be a data glitch. Either way, it shows the rate can swing about 15–20 won within a few days.

**Recent path**
- Oct 1: the won-dollar exchange rate stood at 1,358.4 won at 3:30 p.m. in Seoul.
- Fed H.10 data (US central bank): Oct 5: 1,341.70; Oct 6: 1,337.88; Oct 7: 1,339.12; Oct 8: 1,343.34; Oct 9: 1,342.13.  The rate hovered right around 1,340 in early October.
- Oct 12: The won hit 1,333.2 intraday, the lowest level since October 4, 2024.
- Oct 16: The rate reached 1,328.9 won per dollar at 7:20 p.m.
- Monthly averages: 1,492.5 won in March in the aftermath of the war in the Middle East and to 1,528 won in June, then 1,488.9 in July, 1,404.4 in August and 1,358.8 in September. October so far averages 1,342.6, the strongest since September 2024. 

**What's driving it**
- **Exports:** Booming semiconductor exports are the main driver behind the won's strength.
- **Rate hikes:** Back-to-back base rate increases by the Bank of Korea in July and August widened interest rate differentials, further supporting the won.
- **Against the dollar trend:** The won's strength runs counter to a broader dollar rally that has lifted the dollar index from the 99 level to the 102 level over the past month. That's a risk if the dollar keeps rising.
- **Outlook:** Most forecasts put the won in the low- to mid-1,300s against the dollar by the end of the year.

**Base rate**
The threshold is about 0.4–0.7% above the current level, with 8 trading days to go. A typical USD/KRW move over 8 trading days is roughly 1–2%, so this is well within normal swings. Based on that alone, I'd put the chance of a YES move at roughly 30–40%, adjusted for the downward trend.

**Scheduled events before Oct 29**
- **US Fed meeting:** probably Oct 27–28, ending the day before the resolution date. I haven't confirmed the dates.
- **Bank of Korea:** a rate meeting may fall in late October. I haven't confirmed this either.
- **Korean data:** export figures for the first 20 days of October usually come out around Oct 21. Korean GDP figures for the third quarter come out in late October.
- **Geopolitics:** Middle East and oil-price risk pushed the won weaker earlier this year.

I found no prediction markets on this question.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the USD/KRW exchange rate (South Korean won per one US dollar) reported by Trading Economics at https://tradingeconomics.com/south-korea/currency for October 29, 2026 is greater than 1,340.00 (i.e. the won is weaker/more depreciated than 1,340 per dollar). It resolves NO if that reported rate is 1,340.00 or lower. A reported rate of, for example, 1,355.20 resolves YES; a reported rate of 1,332.10 resolves NO.
letra_pequena: The relevant value is the USD/KRW spot rate shown on the Trading Economics South Korean Won page as the most recent closing value dated October 29, 2026 (Trading Economics reports this figure in its page text, e.g. "The USD/KRW exchange rate fell to 1,339.2700 on October 14, 2026"). If Trading Economics does not report a value dated October 29, 2026 (for instance due to a data gap), the closing USD/KRW spot rate for October 29, 2026 from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as Wise or Investing.com will be used. If no closing value for that date is available from any such source, the question is annulled.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** Ten calendar days, or about eight trading sessions, until the October 29 close.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. The latest quoted rate is around 1,330–1,335, below 1,340.

(c) **Reference class:** For an exchange rate this close to a threshold over roughly eight sessions, ordinary fluctuations can cross it. Given the recent strengthening trend, I’d put the base rate for finishing above 1,340 at roughly one in three.

(d) **NO scenario:** Export strength and a steady or softer dollar keep USD/KRW at or below 1,340.

(e) **YES scenario:** A Fed surprise, renewed foreign equity selling, or a broader dollar rise pushes USD/KRW back above 1,340.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The test is the **October 29 closing rate reported by Trading Economics**, not an intraday crossing. Exactly 1,340.00 resolves NO; another credible source is used only if Trading Economics lacks a value for that date.

Probability: 37%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 calendar days, or roughly 8 trading days, until the October 29, 2026 close.

(b) **Status quo:** Spot is about 1,330–1,335. Trading Economics shows 1,334.55 and Wise shows 1,330.2. Both are below 1,340, so the status quo resolves NO, but the margin is only about 0.4–0.7%.

(c) **Reference class:** USD/KRW moves over about 8 trading days.
- Daily volatility is roughly 0.5%, which gives an 8-day standard deviation of about 1.4%, or about 19 won.
- The threshold is 6–10 won above spot, a z-score of about 0.3–0.5.
- That puts the chance of closing above 1,340 at about 31–38%.
- The won has been strengthening over the past month, driven by semiconductor exports and earlier BOK rate hikes, which lowers this somewhat.
- A broader dollar rally (DXY from 99 to 102) and foreign equity outflows push the other way.

(d) **NO scenario:** Strong export data around October 21 keeps exporter dollar supply flowing. The FOMC holds as expected with neutral-to-dovish messaging on October 28. USD/KRW drifts at 1,320–1,338 through October 29.

(e) **YES scenario:** The dollar rally continues, foreign equity selling of Korean stocks intensifies, or the Fed sounds hawkish on October 28. Any of these could push USD/KRW back to the 1,340–1,355 range seen in early October. The Wise 7-day high of 1,351.85 shows swings of that size can happen within days.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- Resolution uses Trading Economics' value dated October 29. Its quotes can be intraday or late-session readings, not the Seoul 3:30 pm close, so the number may differ from the Seoul onshore close by a few won.
- The Fed decision lands on October 28 US time, so its reaction falls in October 29 trading.
- A value of exactly 1,340.00 resolves NO.

Probability: 33%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 calendar days, or eight trading days, from October 19 to October 29.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. The latest quoted rates are below 1,340, around 1,330–1,335.

(c) **Reference class:** For an exchange rate sitting less than 1% from a threshold with eight trading days to go, ordinary short-term fluctuations make a crossing plausible. A rough base rate for finishing above this threshold is **30–40%**, before accounting for the recent trend.

(d) **NO scenario:** The won holds its recent gains, supported by exports or a softer dollar, and USD/KRW closes at or below 1,340.

(e) **YES scenario:** Foreign equity outflows or a Fed-driven dollar rise push USD/KRW back above 1,340 by October 29.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The test is the *reported October 29 closing value*, not an intraday crossing. Exactly **1,340.00 is NO**; only a value greater than 1,340.00 is YES. Trading Economics takes precedence if it reports a value for that date.

The strengthening trend makes NO somewhat more likely than the proximity of the threshold alone would suggest, though the Fed decision leaves meaningful upside risk for USD/KRW.

Probability: 33%
